newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 17.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 17.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
LONDON - Japan's Dentsu Inc, the world's largest advertising agency, has set a sales target of 1.5 trillion yen ($12.9 billion) for the year 2000, president Yutaka Narita says.

SYDNEY - The battle over Olympic marketing takes a new twist as organisers of the Sydney 2000 Games announce an advertising campaign to stem the threat of "ambush marketing" -- or promotional campaigns by companies that do not hold rights to the event.

LONDON - Advertising expenditure in Britain rose across all media in 1996, including a 4.1-percent rise in television to 2.75 billion pounds ($4.6 billion) on an inflation-adjusted basis, a UK trade group the Advertising Association says.
BERLIN - Elf Oil's German unit has awarded its advertising account to the TBWA group, TBWA Germany's chief executive and chairman, Helmut Sendlmeier, says.
LONDON - Advertising group McCann-Erickson's northern UK office is encouraging its staff to take a five-minute swim every day to make them more creative.

PARIS - French advertising agencies saw their gross margins rise 3.4 percent in the first quarter, falling short of their forecast for an increase of four percent for the whole of 1997, the Association des Agences Conseils en Communication says.
LONDON - Maiden Group says it acquired M&M Outdoor Advertising Ltd for 896,868 pounds in cash.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LONDON - Britain's Channel 5 says it has bought the live television rights to Aston Villa's home matches in European soccer's UEFA Cup next season. The deal adds to a growing portfolio of European soccer rights for C5, the fifth terrestrial channel launched four months ago.

FRANKFURT - Germany's top television channel RTL loses ground in June to the ProSieben network, media marketing company IP Deutschland says. RTL sees a drop in ratings to a 15.9 percent viewer share, down from 17 percent in May
LONDON - Britain's Radio Authority says it sees no reason to disallow the proposed acquisition of Virgin Radio, part of Richard Branson's Virgin Group, by Capital Radio.
BALTIMORE, Maryland - Sinclair Broadcast Group Inc says it has entered into an asset purchase agreement to acquire the radio and television stations of Heritage Media Group for $630 million in cash.
WASHINGTON - President Bill Clinton backs private-sector efforts to protect children from Internet smut, without calling for new laws or extensive government intervention in cyberspace.
NEW YORK - Time Warner Inc Chairman Gerald Levin says the company has ended its negotiations with U S West Inc's Media Group and will keep the terms of their partnership intact.
LONDON - Britain's Tourist Authority launches a 40,000-page Internet site in an attempt to promote its thriving tourist industry around the globe.
SINGAPORE - Singapore says it has refused to allow Vogue magazine's British edition for July to be sold in the country because of an article "condoning and promoting the use of drugs".
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - Britain's drinks industry body, the Portman Group, says it has issued a tougher code of practice to retailers and brewers of alcohol in an effort to limit under-age drinking. The industry code will be backed up by government measures aimed at making so-called "alcopops" -- alcoholic lemonade and soda drinks -- less attractive to youngsters.

MUNICH - Troubled Apple Computer Inc. says its units in certain European countries saw third quarter sales in units and revenue rise slightly compared to the second quarter of fiscal year 1997. Sales in Germany and France increased sequentially -- but fell compared to the third quarter of fiscal 1996, Apple spokeswoman Therese Wermelskirchen says.
NEW YORK - Zippo lighters, which have become an American icon, celebrate their 65th anniversary this week.
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's Del Monte Royal Foods Ltd tries to shake off a disastrous trading period by staking its future on a massive European shake-up and casting into new markets for alliances.

LONDON - Britain's Guinness and GrandMet dismiss as too costly and complicated a three-way drinks merger proposal from their largest shareholder, French luxury goods company LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton.

DETROIT - Ford Motor Co. reports the highest quarterly profit in U.S. corporate history. Ford says it earned $2.53 billion in the quarter, surpassing Exxon's Corp.'s fourth quarter 1996 profit of $2.49 billion as the highest on record.
LONDON - British domestic appliance company Kenwood Appliances says it is open to any proposals that could lead to a takeover of the company if it promised value to its shareholders.
BEIJING - China is intensifying its battle to stamp out theft of intellectual property rights but copyright infringement remains widespread, the China Daily says.
BREMEN - Plans by German chocolate manufacturers to raise prices of their products in the autumn may be unrealistic in a competitive environment, a spokesman for Kraft Jacobs Suchardsays
CONSUMER TRENDS:

HELSINKI - American consumers should soon be able to eat fats which reduce their cholesterol levels after a Johnson & Johnson company signs a deal with a firm in Finland which has patented a cholesterol-cutting compound.

BEIJING- In China you can sell T-shirts to make money, but you can't use money to sell T-shirts. China has banned entrepreneurs from using money to decorate T-shirts, baseball hats or any other products saying such acts damage the credibility of the currency, the Xinhua news agency says.
LONDON - Sleepy drivers may be more dangerous than drunk drivers, Australian researchers report.

SHANGHAI - In China, where a preference for bank notes has long held the cashless society at bay, credit cards are gaining popularity, and Shanghai, the country's mercantile hub, is leading the pack, bankers say.
MIAMI BEACH, Florida - Tourist offices in super trendy Miami Beach have been flooded with calls from tourists worried about violence following the murder of designer Gianni Versace.
